### IV.14 (54). 8 April – 12 May 1983 — Registration correspondence

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19830408-1 · Date: 1983-04-08 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

On 8 and 12 April and 12 May 1983 Linklaters and the Land Registry exchange letters on the farmhouse file, including form D23.

> The received account: Routine registration correspondence.
> What we now know: What the Registry asked about the occupiers, and what it was told, is in these letters. The family have asked for them.
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — first registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration

### V.1 (55). 1984 — The writ

Act V: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler · Scene id: ghf-19840522-1 · Date: 1984-05-22 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 22 May 1984 BP Properties issues a writ for possession of Great House Farm and adjoining land against William Buckler. The defence relies on adverse possession from 1955.

> The received account: BP, the owner, sued to recover its land from a squatter.
> Wording: "Great House Farm and adjoining land" — The writ's description.
> Wording: "adverse possession" — The only defence argued.
> What we now know: The house was wrapped back into "the farm" a year after BP registered it separately. BP asked for possession, not a declaration of ownership. The defence fought on BP's map: adverse possession of a synthetic farm whose real owner's title was to Parcel B only, with the clock counted from 1955, when the family's title to Parcel A dated from 1928 and by possession from 1940. In the same year the library copy of the 1877 deed was reported missing.
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — the writ — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#writ
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — library copy missing — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#library-1984
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration

### V.2 (56). 10 July 1986 — High Court judgment

Act V: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler · Scene id: ghf-19860710-1 · Date: 1986-07-10 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 10 July 1986 Mr Justice Hollis gives judgment for BP, holding that the 1974 letters gave Mary a licence.

> The received account: The court found that BP owned the house and the family were there by BP's permission.
> Wording: "licence" — The finding.
> What we now know: The court decided possession. The question of who owned Parcel A was not put to it, and the 1877, 1928 and 1939 documents were not before it.
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — High Court — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#high-court
- Analysis: BP v Buckler: Scope, Decided & Undecided — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/court-judicial-issues/bp-v-buckler-scope-decided-undecided/

### V.3 (57). 1986 – 87 — Royal Commission correspondence

Act V: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler · Scene id: ghf-19860711-1 · Date: 1986-07-11 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

During the trial and appeal, the Royal Commission's correspondence with Mrs Buckler goes missing.

> What we now know: A record of Mary's own account to a public body was lost while the case was live.
- Analysis: Legal Review — the loss pattern — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/#loss-pattern

### V.4 (58). 2 February 1987 — Amalgamation of titles

Act V: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler · Scene id: ghf-19870202-1 · Date: 1987-02-02 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

On 2 February 1987, while the appeal is pending, an application is made to amalgamate WA240304 (the separately registered farmhouse and garden) into WA231076 (the larger field title). The register then presents the two strands as one corporate holding. The affirmative 'synthetic estate' question is whether a title originating in the Bute-to-WGR field chain was joined to a separately registered house title without the older Cydwin/Cydfin and Williams/Thomas chain being traced through the underlying instruments. The amalgamation records a registration event; its file, the 1877 documents, and the 1938 and 1969 conveyances must be read together to reconstruct the title's provenance.

> The received account: An administrative tidying of the register.
> Wording: "amalgamation" — The register's term.
> What we now know: The registration history shows two separately registered titles before the 1987 amalgamation: a larger field title and a later house title. The affirmative synthetic-estate thesis is that a corporate register view was assembled from separate strands while the older Cydwin/Cydfin and Williams/Thomas provenance remained untraced. The decisive exercise is to compare the first-registration files and the operative 1877, 1938 and 1969 instruments against the plans and schedules. The label 'synthetic' describes this unresolved reconstruction, not a statutory finding.
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": Registered: BP Properties, WA231076 = Parcel B + synthetic Parcel A (farmhouse title folded in, 2 February 1987)

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — amalgamation — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Analysis: 1987 HMLR Amalgamation During Appeal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/procedural-fairness-notice/1987-hmlr-amalgamation-during-appeal/
- Wiki page: Cydfin / Ty Mawr and pre-1877 manorial evidence — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/anomalies-register/llandough-penarth-cydfin-ty-mawr-manorial-evidence/
- Research annex: Cedwyn Estate — title-chain reconstruction — https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/research/cedwyn-estate-title-chain.html

### V.5 (59). 31 July 1987 — Court of Appeal

Act V: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler · Scene id: ghf-19870731-1 · Date: 1987-07-31 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 31 July 1987 the Court of Appeal (Dillon LJ, Mustill LJ, Sir Edward Eveleigh) dismisses the appeal in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler. It finds adverse possession from 1955, but holds that the 1962 action stopped time and the 1974 letters made the possession permissive.

> The received account: The courts finally settled that BP owned Great House Farm.
> Wording: "the paper title to the farm" — The court's description of BP's position.
> Wording: "No such documents were, however, ever produced." — On Mary's title documents.
> Wording: "since November 1982 they have been the registered proprietors" — The court's recital.
> What we now know: The court decided possession, not ownership. It counted the clock from 1955, from an order about the fields; counted from 1928, it had run out in 1940. BP's paper title was to the fields; for the house it had only a deed between two BP companies, which the court itself called the conveyance of the farmhouse and garden. Mary's documents were not produced because they had been taken from her. The family lost in the High Court, lost on appeal, and were refused by the Lords. Every defeat was on who may live in the house. Nobody ever asked who owned it.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Billy Buckler · never adjudicated, never extinguished (judgment decides possession only)
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": WA231076, BP Properties · right to possession upheld (1962 order + 1974 licence)

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Analysis: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — what it omits — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#omits

### V.6 (60). 3 March 1988 — House of Lords

Act V: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler · Scene id: ghf-19880303-1 · Date: 1988-03-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 3 March 1988 the House of Lords refuses leave to appeal. The family are given 28 days to leave.

> The received account: The end of the legal road.
> What we now know: The end of the possession case. Ownership of Parcel A had still never been decided.
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — House of Lords — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#house-of-lords

### VI.1 (61). 29 April 1988, morning — First eviction attempt

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19880429-1 · Date: 1988-04-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 29 April 1988 five bailiffs and about fifteen police arrive. William Buckler blocks the drive with a tractor and secures the house.

> The received account: An occupier resisting a lawful order.
> What we now know: Possession was being enforced over a house whose ownership no court had decided.
- Newspaper: 'Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on', c. 30 April 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n07
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 29 April 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-01) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.2 (62). 29 April 1988 — The chainsaw

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19880429-2 · Date: 1988-04-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

The bailiffs break the gate and doors. William Buckler pushes a running chainsaw through a door. After four hours the bailiffs withdraw. BP tells the press Mary had been allowed to stay rent-free because of ill health.

> The received account: The "chainsaw farmer": a violent squatter.
> Wording: "chainsaw farmer" — The headline.
> Wording: "because of her ill health" — BP's account of 1974.
> What we now know: Billy was a father with his three small children behind a door an axe had just come through. The papers called him the chainsaw farmer. Nobody called the men with the axes anything at all. He was defending his home, on land his family had owned since 1928 and lived on since 1667.
- Newspaper: 'Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n07
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 30 April 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-02) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.3 (63). May 1988 — Strasbourg and the MP

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19880512-1 · Date: 1988-05-12 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 3 May 1988 William Buckler applies to the European Commission of Human Rights. On 12 May Alun Michael MP asks the Lord Chancellor to review the case.

> What we now know: Both were pending when the house was demolished.
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 12 May 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-03) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — ECHR — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#echr

### VI.4 (64). 29 July 1988 — Cadw inspection

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19880729-1 · Date: 1988-07-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Photograph

On 29 July 1988 Cadw inspects and photographs the farmhouse and barn while considering them for listing.

> The received account: Cadw looked at the house and found it not good enough to list.
> What we now know: Two photographs survive. There is no file, no notes and no record of who decided.
- Photograph: Cadw survey photograph of the farmhouse, 29 July 1988 (released 2026, ATISN 27021) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/foi-reply-register/#R37
- Photograph: Cadw survey photograph of the barn, 29 July 1988 (released 2026, ATISN 27021) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/foi-reply-register/#R37
- Analysis: Cadw — Forensic Critique — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/cadw-forensic-critique-v8-0-0/

### VI.5 (65). 29 – 30 November 1988 — Eviction

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881130-1 · Date: 1988-11-30 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 29–30 November 1988 bailiffs enter the farmhouse. William Buckler is taken to Llandough Hospital. Eight other residents are made homeless.

> The received account: The lawful owner recovered possession.
> Wording: "possession" — What BP was given.
> What we now know: Billy was hurt and taken to hospital. Eight people lost their homes with the family that day. A family that had lived in the house for three hundred and twenty-one years was put out in an afternoon, by an order that never said whose house it was.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Billy Buckler, evicted 29 November 1988 · never adjudicated, never extinguished
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": WA231076, BP Properties · in possession from 29 November 1988

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo front page — 'Angry scenes as farmer evicted' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n14
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 30 November 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-04) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — 'Billy's unhappy family' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n09

### VI.6 (66). 1 December 1988 — Belongings

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881201-1 · Date: 1988-12-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

The family's belongings, including Mary's papers and photographs, are left in the house or put in the road.

> What we now know: Mary's photographs, the family heirlooms, the papers, everything left of three centuries, in the house or in the road. Whatever remained of the family's own records went with it.
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n08
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 13 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-11) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.7 (67). 2 December 1988 — Injunction

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881202-1 · Date: 1988-12-02 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 2 December 1988 a High Court judge orders that the farmhouse and its contents must not be touched. BP states it plans to demolish and build homes.

> What we now know: The injunction lasted three days.
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — 'History fight to save farm' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n08
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 2 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-05) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.8 (68). 3 December 1988 — Charges

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881209-1 · Date: 1988-12-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

William Buckler is taken from hospital and charged with assaulting two bailiffs, criminal damage, and wanton or furious driving.

> The received account: The violent squatter was charged.
> What we now know: He was taken from his hospital bed and charged. With Billy in hospital, then in the dock, then bailed away from the site, there was no one left standing between BP and the house. Within three days it was gone.
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-06) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n15

### VI.9 (69). 3 – 5 December 1988 — Spot-listing

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881203-1 · Date: 1988-12-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

Over the weekend of 3–5 December 1988 Cadw considers spot-listing without access to the interior.

> The received account: Cadw gave the house fair consideration.
> What we now know: Cadw had already coded the house just below the bar in July.
- Analysis: Cadw — Forensic Critique — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/cadw-forensic-critique-v8-0-0/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — Cadw considering spot-listing — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n08

### VI.10 (70). Monday 5 December 1988 — Final hearing; listing refused

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881205-1 · Date: 1988-12-05 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 5 December 1988 Judge Norman Francis refuses to continue the injunction pending the European Commission. The same day Cadw states the house is not of sufficient merit to list.

> The received account: The house was not worth listing, and the courts had ruled.
> Wording: "not of sufficient architectural merit" — Cadw, 5 December 1988.
> What we now know: On the same day, both doors closed: the court refused to wait for Strasbourg, and Cadw refused to list. Nothing now protected the house, and everyone knew it.
- Newspaper: Western Mail, 6 December 1988 — 'Farmer fails in final eviction hearing' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n10

### VI.11 (71). 6 December 1988, 4am — Demolition

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881206-1 · Date: 1988-12-06 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

From about 4am on 6 December 1988 the farmhouse and buildings are demolished.

> The received account: An old farmhouse of no special merit was cleared for housing.
> Wording: "Bulldozed before breakfast" — The headline.
> Wording: "suddenly and completely destroyed" — The Royal Commission's archive record (NMR 6048945).
> What we now know: At four in the morning, in the dark, before anyone could stop it. Branwen and her three small children watched their home come down. A thousand people had signed to save it. An MP had asked for the case to be looked at again. Strasbourg had not yet heard it. None of it mattered by breakfast. The house was destroyed before it was ever fully recorded. The title to Parcel A was not destroyed with it.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Billy Buckler · house demolished 6 December 1988 · title never adjudicated, never extinguished

- Newspaper: 'Tears flow as 800 year-old farm house is razed at last' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n11
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 6 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-07) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 21 December 1988 (reader's letter on "Bulldozed Before Breakfast") (search extract GHF-E090-N15-12) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s

### VI.12 (72). 7 – 9 December 1988 — Local reaction and bail

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881208-1 · Date: 1988-12-07 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

A Vale of Glamorgan councillor calls the demolition "disgusting". Villagers meet their councillors on 8 December. On 9 December William Buckler is bailed on condition he stays away from the site.

> What we now know: He was barred from the land his family had owned.
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 7 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-08) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 9 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-09) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 10 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-10) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Wiki page: 1988: Possession and Demolition — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/demolition-1988/

### VI.13 (73). December 1988 — Royal Commission in the rubble

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881212-1 · Date: 1988-12-12 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Heritage record

An examination of the rubble, recorded in the heritage record, notes a fireplace jamb and an ogee-stopped beam with torus, and the loss of the carved stone capital kept by the front door.

> The received account: A minor record of a lost farmhouse.
> What we now know: Evidence of a house of quality, recorded only after it was destroyed.
- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s

On 20 March 1989 lorries clear the site.

### VII.2 (75). January – March 1989 — Charges resolved

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19890323-1 · Date: 1989-03-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

In January 1989 one charge is dropped as out of time and William Buckler is barred from within half a mile of the site. On 23 March he pleads guilty to the remaining charges and is freed.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 23 March 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-15) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VII.3 (76). 1989 — Rehousing

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19890325-1 · Date: 1989-03-25 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

The family live with William Buckler's sister in Penarth. He plans to live in a converted bus and says about £30,000 of possessions were taken from the site.

> What we now know: The family who had lived in the Great House for three centuries were now planning to live in a bus.
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 1989 — 'From farm to a bus' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n13

### VII.4 (77). 14 April 1989 — European Commission decision

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19890414-1 · Date: 1989-04-14 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 14 April 1989 the European Commission of Human Rights declares Buckler v United Kingdom inadmissible.

> The received account: Strasbourg confirmed the eviction was lawful and the property was BP's.
> Wording: "the property belonged to another" — The Commission's reading of the domestic judgments.
> What we now know: Strasbourg relied on the British courts, which had decided possession, not ownership. It never saw a title deed. Another loss, on a question nobody had ever asked.
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — ECHR — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#echr
- Court record: Buckler v United Kingdom, Commission decision (PDF) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/wp-1790112811838.pdf

### VII.5 (78). October – November 1989 — Outline application

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19891107-1 · Date: 1989-11-07 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

BP applies for outline planning permission for housing (89/01396/OUT, received 8 November 1989). In the same document GGAT advises an archaeological assessment, prices the work at £2,000 and discloses negotiations with BP's agents; it is then commissioned to carry out the assessment. GGAT's 1989 planning report describes the farmhouse as having been listed as a "county treasure"; Cadw states it was never listed.

> The received account: Routine planning with archaeological advice.
> What we now know: The adviser to the council became the developer's contractor on the same site.
- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings
- Analysis: Source Conflicts Register — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/source-conflicts-register/

### VII.6 (79). February – March 1990 — Outline permission

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19900313-1 · Date: 1990-03-13 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

On 13 March 1990 outline permission is granted with 18 conditions. The officer's report notes the farm buildings "were unfortunately demolished a little while ago". GGAT's further comments of 8 February 1990 are missing from the file.

> Wording: "unfortunately demolished" — The officer's report.
> What we now know: The Local Plan had required the buildings to be kept. No preservation notice had been served.

### VII.7 (80). 29 May 1990 — Death of William Buckler

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19900529-1 · Date: 1990-05-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Source pending (date corrected from family information)

William Buckler died on 29 May 1990 at Llandough Hospital. Funeral and burial details require confirmation against the obituary and relevant records.

> What we now know: He was in his forties. He died in the village where he was born, without his home, without ever having had the one question that mattered answered. Mary's claim to the house passed, undecided, to his children.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Mary's heirs · never adjudicated, never extinguished

- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — William — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### VII.8 (81). August – October 1990 — Evaluation trenches

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19900801-1 · Date: 1990-08-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

In August 1990 GGAT digs eight trenches for BP and finds early medieval burials. An area that could not be investigated is marked low potential. In October the council records the condition as met.

> Wording: "low potential" — GGAT's zoning.
> What we now know: The 1994 excavation found burials in the area marked low potential.
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### VII.13 (86). December 1993 — Transfer to Ideal Homes

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19931203-1 · Date: 1993-12-03 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

On 3 December 1993 BP transfers the site to Ideal Homes and groundworks begin. On 13 December GGAT asks the council for a breach-of-condition notice. The council accepts the developer's counsel's opinion that the condition is discharged.

> The received account: BP sold its land to a developer.
> Wording: "a difference of opinion" — The council to the MP.
> What we now know: The merged title, including the synthetic Parcel A, passed to a buyer as though it were one parcel.
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": WA231076 transferred by BP to Ideal Homes (December 1993); later Persimmon Homes (Wales)

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.14 (87). March – July 1994 — Cemetery excavation

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19940504-1 · Date: 1994-03-21 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

March–July 1994: the Cotswold Archaeological Trust excavates an early medieval cemetery on the site. Published totals reach 1,026 burials. The Home Office licence lapsed between 21 April and at least 3 May while work continued.

> The received account: A successful rescue excavation.
> Wording: "preservation by record" — The agreed basis of the excavation.
> What we now know: The largest early medieval burial population then recovered in Wales, from ground marked low potential in 1990.
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/

### VII.15 (88). 28 July 1994 — Finds to the National Museum

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19940728-1 · Date: 1994-07-28 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Museum record

On 28 July 1994 Ideal Homes Wales, as landowner, gives the human remains and finds to the National Museum of Wales (95.56H).

> The received account: The landowner donated the finds.
> Wording: "as landowner" — The basis of the gift.
> What we now know: Ownership of finds follows ownership of land. The finds from Parcel A were given away on the strength of the merged title.
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.16 (89). 1994 – 96 — Woodland title and houses

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19941110-1 · Date: 1994-11-10 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

On 10 November 1994 the woodland passes to the Forest of Cardiff (WA735527). In 1995–96 rights are granted to South Wales Electricity. The houses of Church View Close are built.

> What we now know: The Forest of Cardiff says it bought the woodland in 1994. Per the Buckler case, this woodland, part of Parcel A, had been taken in 1955, and the charity has not used it. (SOURCE PENDING: not yet recorded on the wiki.)
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Mary's heirs · never adjudicated, never extinguished · woodland now registered to the Forest of Cardiff (WA735527) · land to the south a village green
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": WA231076 and the house titles carved from it (Church View Close)

- Wiki page: Woodland — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings
- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/

### VII.17 (90). 2005 — Publication

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-20050101-1 · Date: 2005-01-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

The excavation is published in Medieval Archaeology 49 (2005): 1,026 burials, 814 articulated. On 22 December 2005 part of the woodland title is divided off.

> What we now know: The publication does not mention the family or the house's demolition.

### VIII.2 (93). February – March 2026 — Land Registry reply

Act VIII: Records · Scene id: ghf-20260323-1 · Date: 2026-03-23 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

On 23 March 2026 HM Land Registry sets out the registration history and states there is "no evidence of a mistake in the register".

> The received account: The register is right.
> Wording: "no evidence of a mistake in the register" — HMLR, 23 March 2026.

### VIII.3 (94). 19 April – 25 May 2026 — Complaint decisions

Act VIII: Records · Scene id: ghf-20260419-1 · Date: 2026-04-19 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

On 19 April 2026 HM Land Registry refuses the stage-one complaint. On 25 May the stage-two decision states the title is "registered correctly".

> The received account: The matter has been examined and closed.
> Wording: "registered correctly" — HMLR, 25 May 2026.
> What we now know: The decisions rely on the 1987 judgment, which decided possession, to answer a question of ownership.
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": Land Registry, May 2026: 'registered correctly'

### VIII.4 (95). 21 May 2026 — Cadw disclosure

Act VIII: Records · Scene id: ghf-20260521-1 · Date: 2026-05-21 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

On 21 May 2026 Cadw releases two photographs of 29 July 1988, coded "YYY", which it describes as "marginally below the bar"; on 10 July it says the code meant the building did not meet the criteria. It says its paper file is "quite likely" destroyed, and later "most likely"; it holds no destruction record.

> The received account: The house was assessed and narrowly failed.
> Wording: "marginally below the bar" — Cadw's reading of YYY.
> What we now know: There is no record of the file's destruction.
- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/
- Analysis: Cadw — Forensic Critique — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/cadw-forensic-critique-v8-0-0/
- Photograph: Cadw survey photograph of the farmhouse, 29 July 1988 (released 2026, ATISN 27021) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/foi-reply-register/#R37
- Analysis: Source Conflicts Register — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/source-conflicts-register/

### VIII.13 (104). September – October 2026 — HER source-file digitisation and publication

Act VIII: Records · Scene id: ghf-20261006-1 · Date: 2026-10-06 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

The public HER entry GGAT02038s already referred to H. J. Thomas's 1974 survey and cited R. F. Suggett's December 1988 note. Following the family's September 2026 records request, Heneb reportedly stated on 14 October that the underlying source file had been digitised and uploaded to Archwilio as PDFs in the sources section. Heneb responded to the schedule of records on 16 October. This distinguishes the earlier public citation from the later availability of the underlying source-file material; it does not by itself establish concealment or what the Strasbourg Commission received.

> What we now know: No deed has been produced by which Parcel A passed from the Williamses, or from anyone, to BP.

### O.1 (105). Plainly — They were not squatters

Stating the obvious: Stating the obvious · Scene id: ghf-obvious-01 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Analysis

The Williams family lived at Great House from 1667 to 1988.

> The received account: A squatter was evicted after losing in court.
> Wording: "squatter" — How the case was understood in the press and in the street.
> What we now know: A squatter moves into a place that is not theirs. The Williamses were born in this house, married in it and died in it for three hundred and twenty-one years. On Mary's statement they owned it from 1928, and on the family's case by possession from 1940. Nobody who lives somewhere for three centuries is a squatter.
- Mary's statement: Mary (Nancy) Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### O.2 (106). Plainly — Mary never asked for permission

Stating the obvious: Stating the obvious · Scene id: ghf-obvious-02 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Analysis

Mary (Nancy) Williams refused the tenancies offered in 1959 and 1965 and did not accept the 1974 letters.

> The received account: She lived there by the landlord's permission.
> Wording: "licence" — 1974; relied on in 1986 and 1987.
> What we now know: You cannot be given permission you refuse. Every offer of a tenancy, and the licence, was an attempt to turn an owner into a guest in her own house. She said no every time.
- Court record: The 1959 refusal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#refusal-1959
- Wiki page: The 1965 offer — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#offer-1965
- Court record: The 1974 Licence Letters — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#letters

### O.3 (107). Plainly — Nobody produced a deed to the house

Stating the obvious: Stating the obvious · Scene id: ghf-obvious-03 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Analysis

No conveyance of the farmhouse parcel to Western Ground Rents or to BP, earlier than the 1975 conveyance between two BP companies, has been produced.

> The received account: BP owned the farm.
> Wording: "the paper title to the farm" — Court of Appeal, 1987.
> What we now know: If Western Ground Rents or BP had a deed to the house, they would have produced it at the first hearing and the case would have been over in a day. They used tenancy offers, orders, a licence and their own conveyance instead. People with deeds don't need tricks.
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — conveyances — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#conveyances

### O.4 (108). Plainly — They knew it was two parcels

Stating the obvious: Stating the obvious · Scene id: ghf-obvious-04 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Analysis

In 1983 BP registered the farmhouse and garden as a separate title. In 1987 it was amalgamated with the main title.

> The received account: It was always one farm.
> Wording: "the whole farm" — 1916 onwards.
> What we now know: You cannot merge two titles unless there are two. BP knew. The Land Registry knew. The court read a separate conveyance of the farmhouse and garden. The only people never told what that meant were the family.
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — first registration and amalgamation — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration

### O.5 (109). Plainly — Losing on possession is not losing on ownership

Stating the obvious: Stating the obvious · Scene id: ghf-obvious-05 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Analysis

The High Court (1986), the Court of Appeal (1987), the House of Lords (1988) and the European Commission of Human Rights (1989) ruled against the family on possession.

> The received account: They lost every case, so they must have been wrong.
> Wording: "lost" — Every headline.
> What we now know: They lost every round of an argument about who could live in the house. Nobody ever asked who owned it. You can lose a hundred times on the wrong question and still be right about the real one.
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Analysis: BP v Buckler: Scope, Decided & Undecided — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/court-judicial-issues/bp-v-buckler-scope-decided-undecided/

### O.6 (110). Plainly — William Buckler was the last obstacle

Stating the obvious: Stating the obvious · Scene id: ghf-obvious-06 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Analysis

William Buckler was injured during the eviction of 29–30 November 1988, charged from hospital on 3 December, and bailed on 9 December on condition he stayed away from the site. The house was demolished on 6 December.

> The received account: A violent man was arrested and charged.
> Wording: "chainsaw farmer" — The headline.
> What we now know: He physically stood in their way, so he was removed: to hospital, to the dock, then barred from the site by his bail. With him out of the way there was nobody left between BP and the house. It came down within the week.
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo — 'Angry scenes as farmer evicted' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n14
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-06) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 9 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-09) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### O.7 (111). Plainly — Four in the morning was chosen

Stating the obvious: Stating the obvious · Scene id: ghf-obvious-07 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Analysis

Listing was refused on 5 December 1988. Demolition began at about 4am on 6 December. The European Commission application was pending.

> The received account: An old building was cleared for housing.
> Wording: "suddenly and completely destroyed" — The Royal Commission's archive record (NMR 6048945).
> What we now know: You don't start bulldozers at four in the morning by accident. It was done in the dark, the morning after the last protection fell and before Strasbourg could be heard, so that it could not be stopped and could never be undone.
- Newspaper: 'Tears flow as 800 year-old farm house is razed at last' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n11
- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s

### O.8 (112). Plainly — The public was on their side

Stating the obvious: Stating the obvious · Scene id: ghf-obvious-08 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Analysis

In 1974 about 1,000 people signed a petition to save the house. In 1988 villagers protested the demolition and an MP asked for the case to be reviewed.

> The received account: Nobody much cared about an old farmhouse.
> What we now know: The public stood with the family. A thousand signatures, an MP, a furious village. It made no difference. Where the public could not be persuaded, force and stealth were used instead.
- Newspaper: Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n03
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 12 May 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-03) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 7 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-08) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### O.9 (113). Plainly — The papers did not leave on their own

Stating the obvious: Stating the obvious · Scene id: ghf-obvious-09 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Analysis

Mary (Nancy) Williams's statement records that the family papers were taken from the blanket box in 1950–52 by a lodger placed in the house by an estate agent, and given to the agent.

> The received account: If they ever had papers, they couldn't produce them.
> Wording: "never produced" — Court of Appeal, 1987.
> What we now know: Title deeds don't walk out of a blanket box. They were taken, by a man an estate agent put in the house, and handed to that agent. Thirty-five years later a court noted that they had never been produced.
- Mary's statement: Mary (Nancy) Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — papers taken — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#papers-taken

### O.10 (114). Plainly — A decision with no file

Stating the obvious: Stating the obvious · Scene id: ghf-obvious-10 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Analysis

Cadw holds two photographs of 29 July 1988 and no other record of its 1988 listing consideration.

> The received account: Cadw assessed the house properly and it fell just short.
> Wording: "marginally below the bar" — Cadw, 2026.
> What we now know: A public body decided the fate of a three-hundred-year-old house and kept no file, no notes and no name. A decision nobody can examine is a decision nobody can challenge.
- Photograph: Cadw survey photograph of the farmhouse, 29 July 1988 (released 2026, ATISN 27021) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/foi-reply-register/#R37
- Analysis: Cadw — Forensic Critique — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/cadw-forensic-critique-v8-0-0/

### O.11 (115). Plainly — They never asked a court who owned the house

Stating the obvious: Stating the obvious · Scene id: ghf-obvious-11 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Analysis

BP's 1974 action, in which Mary pleaded ownership, was adjourned and not relisted. The 1984 writ sought possession, not a declaration of ownership.

> The received account: The courts settled who owned Great House Farm.
> What we now know: In 1974 the question of ownership was in front of a judge, and BP walked away from it. In 1984 it asked only for possession. If you were sure you owned the house, you would ask a court to say so. They never did.
- Court record: The 1974 Licence Letters — the action — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#action
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — the writ — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#writ

### E.1 (116). Today — The sequence

Epilogue: Today · Scene id: ghf-99990101-1 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Analysis

1916 to 1987: a tenancy, two possession orders, three tenancy offers, licence letters, a conveyance, two registrations and an amalgamation.

> The received account: A landlord and its successors recovered their farm from tenants who stayed on without paying, and the courts confirmed it.
> Wording: "the whole farm" — 1916.
> Wording: "the whole of the farm" — 1955.
> Wording: "licence" — 1974.
> Wording: "the paper title to the farm" — 1987.
> Wording: "registered correctly" — 2026.
> What we now know: Parcel A was the family's from 1928, and by possession from 1940. It was never shown to belong to Western Ground Rents or BP. A synthetic single farm was described in 1916; six attempts (1949, 1955, 1959, 1962, 1965, 1974) treated Mary's occupation as permissive; the woodland and the land to the south were taken; the 1975 conveyance and 1983 registration gave the synthetic Parcel A a deed and a title; the 1987 amalgamation folded it into Parcel B. The courts decided possession and never decided ownership. Possession can be awarded without ownership being tried, and land can be registered without a rival claim being decided. Neither decides the older title.
- Wiki page: The Two Parcels — the title test — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/the-two-parcels/
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### E.2 (117). Today — The two parcels in the record

Epilogue: Today · Scene id: ghf-99990101-4 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Analysis

Records of 1877–1987 describe the property both as one farm and as separate parts.

> The received account: It was always one farm, and nobody suggested otherwise.
> Wording: "the whole farm" — One farm.
> Wording: "the farmhouse and garden" — One part, named on its own.
> What we now know: Mary's 1974 statement describes the 1877 split; no lawyer of hers built a case on it. Western Ground Rents offered tenancies of, and sued for, the farmhouse and garden alone. BP conveyed it alone in 1975, registered it alone in 1983, and merged it in 1987. The Land Registry held two titles and joined them. The Court of Appeal read a conveyance of the farmhouse and garden. Those who knew the parcels were separate treated them as one where that helped and as two where that helped. The family's case is that this was a conspiracy against them.
- Mary's statement: Mary (Nancy) Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The Two Parcels — the title test — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/the-two-parcels/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — two titles, then one — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

### E.3 (118). Today — The site today

Epilogue: Today · Scene id: ghf-99990101-2 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Analysis

Church View Close, twenty houses, stands on the site. The woodland is registered to the Forest of Cardiff. The human remains are held by the National Museum of Wales.

> The received account: A modern estate on a former farm.
> What we now know: The title to Parcel A has never been decided and never extinguished.
- Wiki page: Where Things Stand — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/
- Wiki page: Missing Records Register — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/missing-records-register/

### E.4 (119). Today — Village history

Epilogue: Today · Scene id: ghf-99990101-3 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Public record

Llandough Community Council's page on the village's history describes the Roman villa and the 1994 burials. It does not mention Great House, the Williams family or the demolition.

> What we now know: There has been no public inquiry, apology or reparation.
- Public record: Llandough Community Council — About Llandough — https://www.llandough-cc.co.uk/About_Us_20117.aspx
- Wiki page: Where Things Stand — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/

### E.5 (120). Today — The family's requests

Epilogue: Today · Scene id: ghf-99990102-1 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family case

The family ask for: a ruling on the ownership of Parcel A; the return of the woodland and the green, or reparation; reparation for the houses built on the land; the return of the estate's artefacts; a true heritage record; and a public inquiry.

> What we now know: Every body involved is being given the opportunity to put it right before the family return to court.
- Wiki page: Family Reparations & Remedy Roadmap — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/family-reparations-remedy-roadmap/
- Wiki page: Where Things Stand — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/
